problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
raw_comments: we can solve this using a min heap of size k
since we want the kth largest element, we push values that are larger than the current value
and then by the end the kth largest value should just be the value sitting on top of the heap
initialize the heap of size k
go thorugh the rest of the elements
if the current num is greater than the value at the top of the heap
divergences:
none really, just had to remember the heap syntax
TC:
building heap takes O(k) time
traversing the heap and using the operations heappushpop is O(logk) (traversing the tree)
O(nlogk) and space is just O(k)

problems.title: Daily Temperatures
raw_comments: we can use a stack for this question storing the index of the temperature
we store the days that have not resolved when there is a warmer temp

then we go through the temperatures and compare; if the temperature is hotter than the one on the stack, we pop the index and append the difference between the current temp and the temp on the stack to resolve it
if the current temperature is hotter than the temperature on the top of the stack
pop it and then append the result to the idx of the temperature on the stack because we found a hotter day
divergences:
just misrepresented the stack
stack should represent the index of unresolved temps and not the temps themselves
TC: O(n) b/c push pop are O(1) but we traverse through the whole list
SC: O(n) b/c we store all the idx at most once

problems.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
raw_comments: divergences:
none
stacks are LIFO and queues are FIFO so appending all items in one stack to another reverses this and gives us the proper behavior we want for a queue
Your MyQueue object will be instantiated and called as such:
obj = MyQueue()
obj.push(x)
param_2 = obj.pop()
param_3 = obj.peek()
param_4 = obj.empty()
